title: Jira Free Plan: Limits and What the 11th User Costs
snippet:
**Short answer:** yes, Jira is free for up to **10 users** with **no time limit** and no credit card. The Free plan gives you projects, boards, backlogs, timelines and automation, but caps storage at 2 GB, email at 100 a day and automation at 150 steps a month for the whole site, and it has no permissions, no roles and no Rovo AI. The 11th user starts a 7-day Standard trial; after it you pay for all 11: **$106.70 a month** or **$1,450 a year**. Apps follow the same count, so three common apps add about $640 a year at 11 users.

| Limit | Free | Standard | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Users | 10 | up to 100,000 | pricing page |
| Time limit | none (“Free forever for 10 users”) | paid | pricing page |
| Storage | 2 GB | 250 GB | pricing page |
| Email notifications | 100 emails per day for the whole site | unlimited | pricing page, support |
| Automation | 150 automation steps per month for the site | 400 steps per user per month | pricing page |
| Permissions and roles | none: “everyone with access to Jira is an admin for all Jira spaces” | user roles and permissions | support page |
| Guests, anonymous access | no | free guests (up to 5 per paid user), anonymous access | pricing page, guest docs |
| Audit logs | no | site changes | support page |
| Rovo AI (search, chat, agents) | “The Free plan does not include Rovo.” | 25 Rovo credits per user per month | pricing FAQ |
| Rovo MCP server | not listed on Free | included | pricing compare table |
| Support | Atlassian Community | local business hours | pricing page |

Atlassian’s calculator on 5 November 2026. Monthly billing charges for “the exact number of Jira users you have”; annual billing charges “the tier that most closely matches your user count”.
| Users | Standard, monthly | Standard, annual | Premium, monthly | Premium, annual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | $0 (Free) | $0 (Free) | n/a | n/a |
| 11 | 11 × $9.70 = **$106.70** | **$1,450** (tier 11 to 15) | 11 × $19.60 = $215.60 | $2,950 |
| 25 | 25 × $9.70 = **$242.50** | **$2,450** (tier 16 to 25) | 25 × $19.60 = $490 | $4,900 |
| 50 | 50 × $9.70 = **$485** | **$4,850** (tier 26 to 50) | 50 × $19.60 = $980 | $9,800 |

Both. Jira Cloud has a Free plan for up to 10 users that Atlassian calls "free forever", with no credit card. Above 10 users you need a paid plan: Standard was $9.70 per user per month on monthly billing on 5 November 2026, Premium $19.60. Annual billing is by tier, for example $1,450 a year for 11 to 15 users on Standard.

title: Jira Pricing: How Much Does Jira Cost in 2026?
snippet:
- **Jira Cloud has four plans.** At 100 users, Standard costs $9.05 per user per month and Premium $18.30. Free covers up to 10 users. Enterprise is annual only and starts at $166,000 a year for 801+ users.
- **Annual billing can save you up to 17%, but there is a caveat.** Monthly pricing rises with every seat you add, while annual pricing is sold in fixed user tiers. Where your headcount sits inside its tier decides which option wins.

To serve a wide variety of organizations, Atlassian offers Jira Cloud in four pricing tiers: Free, Standard, Premium, and Enterprise. The table below describes the key differences.
| Jira Cloud pricing tiers (August 2026) | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plans | Free | Standard | Premium | Enterprise |
| Pricing, per user/month (100 users) | $0 | $9.05 | $18.30 | Not available |
| Pricing, annual (100 users) | $0 | $9,050 | $18,300 | Not available for 100 users |
| User limit per site | 10 users | 100,000 users | 100,000 users | 100,000 users |
| Number of sites | 1 | 1 | 1 | Up to 150 |
| File storage | 2 GB | 250 GB | Unlimited storage | Unlimited storage |
| Dependency management | Single project | Single project | Cross-project (Jira Plans) | Cross-project (Jira Plans) |
| Atlassian Rovo |

- **Free suits a single team of up to 10 people running straightforward workflows, and teams evaluating Jira before committing.** No cap on work items or spaces, but the features you get access to are pretty basic: limited storage and automation rule runs, no dedicated support or AI features, no user roles and permissions, etc.
